explain_certara_workflow("fit a base PK model") #> [[1]] #> [[1]]$id #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.pkpd_end_to_end" #>  #> [[1]]$title #> [1] "Default end-to-end PK/PD workflow" #>  #> [[1]]$summary #> [1] "Recommended order - EDA, base structural model selection, covariate search, final fit, GOF and VPC - each in its own run folder." #>  #> [[1]]$details_md #> [1] "A typical RsNLME modeling sequence (PK, PD, or PK/PD - the steps are the same
for every model family, only the constructor changes):

1. Exploratory data analysis of the dataset (doses, observations, covariates).
2. Pick a structural model: choose a built-in constructor that matches
   (`pkmodel`, `pklinearmodel`, `pkindirectmodel`, `pkemaxmodel`, `emaxmodel`,
   `linearmodel` - see `list_builtin_model_constructors`) or, when no built-in
   template fits the requested structure, build custom PML with `textualmodel()`
   after `validate_pml()`. Map columns inline or with `colMapping()`.
   Optionally add derived reporting parameters with `addSecondary()` on the
   builtin model object (e.g. after `pkmodel(...)`: half-lives, micro/macro
   bridges, `Vss`) before fitting — secondaries are computed at fit time and
   cannot be added to an existing fit. Prefer fixef-only expressions; see
   `Certara.RsNLME.pml.secondary` and `Certara.RsNLME.pml.secondary_catalog`.
3. Fit each candidate with `fitmodel()`; compare on -2LL/AIC. Use sensible
   initials (see `workflow.initial_estimates`). The result is the **structural
   base model**: IIV and residual error, no estimated covariate effects (fixed
   structural scaling/required design effects aside). A reference/literature
   model with covariates is not the base - see `guidance.topic.model_stages`.
4. Begin the **covariate model**: branch the settled base with `copyModel()` and
   add covariate effects via `addCovariate()`/`covariateModel()`.
5. Run `stepwiseSearch()` (or `shotgunSearch()`) for covariate selection - see
   `workflow.choose_run_mode` for when each applies.
6. Final fit; assess GOF with `Certara.Xpose.NLME` - build an xpdb
   (`xposeNlme(dir = run_dir)`), then GOF plots + `get_summaryNlme()`, see
   `workflow.gof_xpose` - and run `vpcmodel()` + tidyvpc. Optionally `bootstrap()`
   for parameter uncertainty, summarized with `get_bootSummaryNlme()` (see
   `workflow.bootstrap_summary_xpose`).

For headless/agent use, build the model and fit in one job with
`start_nlme_fit_spec`, or iterate with `start_nlme_fitmodel`; keep each step in
its own working directory for reproducibility." #>  #> [[1]]$parent #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.toc" #>  #> [[1]]$steps #> NULL #>  #> [[1]]$related #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.pkmodel"                       #> [2] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.stepwiseSearch"                #> [3] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.vpcmodel"                      #> [4] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.gof_xpose"               #> [5] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.bootstrap_summary_xpose" #>  #>  #> [[2]] #> [[2]]$id #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.mcp.bundled_scripts" #>  #> [[2]]$title #> [1] "Bundled MCP job scripts (compare, SCM, data prep, VPC, bootstrap, simulation)" #>  #> [[2]]$summary #> [1] "The package ships ready-to-run R scripts under inst/mcp/scripts for multi-step workflows; run them with start_nlme_job(file = ...) instead of hand-writing R, passing inputs via environment variables." #>  #> [[2]]$details_md #> [1] "Prefer these bundled scripts over writing R by hand. Run with
`start_nlme_job(file = "<script>.R")`; each script reads its inputs from
environment variables and writes artifacts under `<RUN_DIR>/artifacts`.

| Script | Purpose | Key inputs (env vars) |
|--------|---------|-----------------------|
| `examples/prepare_pk_data.R` | Clean/assemble a PK dataset (writes a prepared CSV) | dataset path + mapping vars |
| `compare_models.R` | Compare two fits on -2LL/AIC/BIC | `FIT_RDS_A`, `FIT_RDS_B` |
| `scm_stepwise.R` | Stepwise covariate search (forward add + backward eliminate) | base model + covariate scenarios |
| `scm_shotgun.R` | Exhaustive all-combinations covariate search (grows as 2^n) | base model + covariate scenarios |
| `covariate_grid.R` | Fit a small, prespecified grid of covariate models and rank them | `GRID_SPEC` (JSON: `base` fit-spec + named `recipes`) |
| `vpc.R` | Visual predictive check from a fit | `FIT_RDS` |
| `bootstrap.R` | Bootstrap a final model for parameter uncertainty | `MODEL_RDS` (the fitted model, e.g. `fit$model`), `BOOT_PARAMS_RDS` |
| `simulation.R` | Simulate from a model | model + simulation spec |
| `population_fit.R`, `naive_pooled_fit.R` | Single-model fits | model + method |

Notes:

- Prefer the first-class `start_nlme_bootstrap` tool over running `bootstrap.R`
  directly: it always reroots into its own run sandbox (see artifact-safety
  guidance) and reads the same `MODEL_RDS` input, so the parent fit's
  `dmp.txt`/`residuals.csv` are never at risk of being overwritten.
- `compare_models.R` reports the numbers only; a likelihood-ratio comparison is
  valid for nested models on the same data, while non-nested candidates are
  compared on AIC/BIC. The newer `compare_nlme_jobs` tool ranks several jobs at
  once and is the preferred entry point for multi-model comparison.
- `covariate_grid.R` fits an explicit, prespecified set of covariate models
  (e.g. base, weight-only, full) so the warfpk-style comparison runs without
  writing R; it is NOT a search. For covariate selection across many candidate
  effects use `scm_stepwise.R`. The fit-spec `covariates` array is for a single
  prespecified model.
- `prepare_pk_data.R` is the explicit data-writing step; read-only inspection is
  `inspect_pk_dataset`, which never writes files." #>  #> [[2]]$parent #> NULL #>  #> [[2]]$steps #> NULL #>  #> [[2]]$related #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.choose_run_mode" #> [2] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.start_nlme_fit_spec"   #> [3] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.data_eda"        #> [4] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.covariate_model" #>  #>  #> [[3]] #> [[3]]$id #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.fda_poppk_phased" #>  #> [[3]]$title #> [1] "Phased FDA PopPK model building - one job per phase, SCM as its own checkpoint" #>  #> [[3]]$summary #> [1] "Run a regulatory PopPK build as separate, checkpointed jobs - plan, structural base, IIV/BOV/covariance, then SCM as its own long job, then VPC/QPC for the chosen target - watching each job with wait_for_nlme_job and never bundling phases into one monolithic script or polling stdout.log." #>  #> [[3]]$details_md #> [1] "Build a regulatory population PK model as a sequence of **separate, checkpointed
jobs** - never one bundled script. Each phase is launched, watched to terminal,
and collected before the next begins, so a long phase (SCM especially) is a
visible checkpoint and a failure never discards earlier phases.

The single monitoring contract for every job in this playbook is
`start_nlme_*` (launch) -> `wait_for_nlme_job` (until `watch$terminal`) ->
`collect_nlme_job`. Follow each result's `next_action` directive, and stop and
ask the user when a result sets `requires_user_attention`. Never tail
`stdout.log`, never start a shell timer/monitor, and never poll
`get_nlme_job_status` in a loop - watching happens server-side inside
`wait_for_nlme_job`.

1. **Plan first (gate)** - a versioned plan from `save_analysis_plan()` must
   exist before fitting unless `intended_use` is `'exploratory'` or
   `allow_unplanned=TRUE` with a non-empty `unplanned_reason`; otherwise the
   fit/VPC tools refuse to launch
   (`decision.when_to_launch_scm`, `workflow.protocol_to_analysis_plan`). Agree
   one `project_dir` and reuse it for every call
   (`guidance.topic.project_layout`).
2. **Structural base - its own job** - fit candidate structural models with
   `start_nlme_fit_spec` (cold start) or `start_nlme_fitmodel` (iterate a built
   model). This is the structural base: IIV + residual error, no estimated
   covariate effects (`guidance.topic.model_stages`). Watch, collect, and judge
   `fit_health` before moving on.
3. **Random effects / BOV / covariance - its own job(s)** - add IIV structure,
   between-occasion variability, and covariance blocks as separate checkpointed
   fits. Do not fold these into the structural step or into the search.
4. **SCM - its own long job** - run the prespecified covariate search as a single
   dedicated job (`scm_stepwise.R` via `start_nlme_job(file = ...)`, planned and
   gated by `validate_covariate_search`; see
   `workflow.covariate_search_planning`). SCM over a realistic candidate set runs
   for **hours** and tests candidates one at a time - that is normal, not a hang.
   Watch it with `wait_for_nlme_job` like any other job and keep it separate so
   the forward/backward result is a clean, independently collected checkpoint.
5. **VPC / QPC - only after the target is chosen** - run `start_nlme_vpcmodel`
   (pcVPC / QPC) once you know which model you are qualifying: base, final, or
   both. Do not start VPC before the model target is settled.
6. **Models and deliverables** - save portable `.mdl` / `.mmdl` models under
   `<project_dir>/models/`, and let the host capture QC: set
   `certara_session_project_dir` once so the repro script, figures, and report
   accumulate automatically (`workflow.assemble_report`). Report the script and
   report paths at the end.

Anti-pattern this playbook prevents: a single `phases_2_to_7.R` job that bundles
BSV / BOV / covariance / SCM / VPC. That hides the SCM checkpoint, makes a
multi-hour run look like one opaque job, and tempts shell-log polling. Split it -
one job per phase, each watched through MCP." #>  #> [[3]]$parent #> [1] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.toc" #>  #> [[3]]$steps #> NULL #>  #> [[3]]$related #>  [1] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.protocol_to_analysis_plan" #>  [2] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.covariate_search_planning" #>  [3] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.assemble_report"           #>  [4] "Certara.RsNLME.workflow.choose_run_mode"           #>  [5] "Certara.RsNLME.mcp.bundled_scripts"                #>  [6] "Certara.RsNLME.decision.when_to_launch_scm"        #>  [7] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.topic.model_stages"        #>  [8] "Certara.RsNLME.guidance.topic.project_layout"      #>  [9] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.start_nlme_fit_spec"             #> [10] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.start_nlme_vpcmodel"             #> [11] "Certara.RsNLME.fn.save_analysis_plan"              #>  #>
